text.p: A robust trio of metals ended LME ring trading on Thursday with strong gains after gingerly testing higher levels. Zinc climbed to fresh two-year peaks, copper came within a whisker of regaining the $2,300 mark and aluminium wrapped up the day by wiping out more corrective losses.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index was 0.41 points higher at 238.38.

Three months copper closed the afternoon kerb at $2,275 per tonne, up $25, but well off the morning high of $2,295. "It had a good run in the morning, so it wasn't surprising to see some profit-taking," a trader said. Nearby tightness was keeping the market on the boil ahead of Third Wednesday pricing next week, with some shorts waiting until the last minute to cover, analysts said.

Zinc gained $35 or three percent on the day to end at $1,221 after fund buying propelled it above $1,200 in the morning, which in turn triggered stops and fuelled more speculative and technical buying. It ran into strong selling at its high of $1,228, traders said.

Aluminium got a boost from Chinese buying in the afternoon, sending it to a peak of $1,578. The market ended just $2 off the high, a gain on the day of $21. The market has rebounded strongly since bottoming on Tuesday at $1,534 in what analysts called a correction to its four-month uptrend.
Nickel finished the day unchanged at $7,880 after touching $7,940 in the morning.
Lead added $7 to $656 and tin gained $5 to $5,940.
Alloy was indicated higher at $1,490/92 after Wednesday's close of $1,466.

CBOT wheat futures closed higher on prospects for a large sale of U.S. wheat to Pakistan and on news Japan this week bought 120,000 tonnes U.S. wheat. Wheat closed one to two cents higher, with March up 1-3/4 at $3.59 and July ended one cent higher at $3.43 per bushel.

CSCE March world sugar futures closed barely weaker in heavy trade focused on speculative liquation and options activity ahead of Friday's March expiry, market sources said. Spot March settled 0.02 cent weaker at 10.64 cents a pound after trading from 10.73 to 10.53 cents. The outer months ended down 0.03 and 0.04.

New York precious metals futures ended mixed Thursday as the complex digested Wednesday's big gains, but the strength of silver, platinum and palladium was suggesting the year-long decline in gold may be nearing an end, traders said. COMEX April gold ended down $2.40 at $343.00 an ounce after trading from $346.10 to $342.80, within Wednesday's range. Total estimated volume was 35,000 lots. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted at $340.75/25 compared to the London afternoon fix of $342.65 and the New York close Wednesday of $342.80/30.
